translated_text: Tal Auning, January 16, 37. My dear, read carefully! Yesterday I met with my father. He brought me a letter. – Darling, I wrote to you at length from Paris (the 3rd letter). I don't think you received the last one. (8 days after your phone conversation). At least that's what your letter suggests. Of course, I got the beautiful tie, and I kiss you a thousand times for it. And the reasons [illegible]: It wasn't simple. Since he hadn't been in the business, the whole time, and the wonderful work of the inventory and balance sheet remained. I started this work, and no one could have continued it. Postponing this work wouldn't have been possible for tax reasons. Egge's presence certainly wasn't decisive for my question. He wouldn't have finished the work, as he knew little from the last [illegible]. Darling, you scolded me so sweetly. Perhaps you were right about that. I don't know, as I can't judge. Believe me, I wish things were different. But my actions are forced upon me by a situation that, rationally speaking, allows for nothing else. It's perhaps the result of an overly selfish upbringing. A source of pleasure for the parents and a curse for the youth. A cautionary tale for us all. I also wrote to you about London in my last letter. Yes, I'd have to travel by plane because I can't drive through Germany. My visa refusal has already been denied twice. I'll inquire about the options again in Prague. Flying with the French airline is too expensive. But I can only fly via Germany. I haven't been skiing this time. I probably won't get much of a chance. But that's so insignificant in the great chaos I'm currently experiencing. The only bright spot at the moment is a nice, young, very talented director I met and became friends with. He's very capable and runs a modern children's theater in Prague. You know, with shows like "Emil and the Detectives." He also does his own work. He feels exactly the same way I do. He's Czech but lived in Frankfurt. He's just lucky enough to be very rich and can work financially independently. He's also interested in filmmaking and has already written a lot. If you ever have anything, send it to me. I'll also give him the book "The Cadavre en Fin" to read. By the way, I told him a lot about you. Baba, the article is quite good, and I'm glad you had success with it; keep sending me things like that. You'll get it back with your next letter. Maybe again soon.
